---
title: "Name and mark"
description: >-
  Where the name zotLook comes from, the Creole coincidence behind it, and why the mark is a contact sheet shaped into a Z.
---

## The name

**zot** + **Look**.

The obvious part first: *zot* for Zotero, *Look* for Quick Look — the system
preview the plugin drives rather than replaces. The name says what the plugin
does and claims nothing beyond it.

It also names the line it stands in. Mikko Rönkkö's **ZoteroQuickLook** brought
the preview to Zotero 4–6, Guillaume Chapron's **Zotero7QuickLook** to Zotero 7.
Both names were taken, and reusing either would have caused confusion — the more
so because the plugins install side by side. Shortening to **zotLook** keeps the
descent legible without treading on anyone. See [Origins](origins.qmd).

### A coincidence across two languages

Found afterwards rather than intended: **zot** is a word. In Mauritian,
Seychellois and Guianese Creole it is the third- and second-person plural
pronoun — *"they, them"* and *"you, y'all"* — from French *les autres* and *vous
autres*, the initial /z/ carried over from the liaison with the word before it.

::: {.callout-note title="It does not quite hold"}
*"zot look"* reads as **"they look"** — but only by taking one word from each
language. *Look* is English; in Mauritian Creole the verb is *gete*, and the
sentence would be **"zot gete"**.

So it is not a Creole phrase but a meeting of two languages. Found, not made —
and too pleasing to leave out.
:::

The plugin ID is `zotlook@fre.ms`.

## The mark

![](asset/zotlook-logo.svg){width=110}

A **contact sheet**: a 4 × 4 grid of page thumbnails, ten of them marked in the
three highlight colours, and together they form a **Z**.

The choice is not arbitrary. The contact sheet is the one thing this plugin
builds that no file manager hands you, so the mark shows what it contributes
rather than only what it depends on. And the Z answers the question about Zotero
without borrowing a line of its logo.

### Why it works without colour

The letter is carried by **marked against unmarked**, not by hue. It therefore
survives greyscale, a dark background and colour blindness alike. For the same
reason the six unmarked tiles stay pale rather than dropping out — they are the
ground the Z is read against.

### Why every size is drawn separately

Not scaled from one file, but each on its own pixel grid:

| Size | for |
|---|---|
| **24 px** | the preferences sidebar — Zotero's stylesheet puts `#prefs-navigation>richlistitem image` at that width |
| **32 px** | the add-ons list |
| **96 px** | that same list on a 2× display |

Only at 96 px is there room for the outlines and the suggested lines of text.
Below it they close up into grey, so there the unmarked tiles are a flat pale
fill.

### Why it carries its own colour

Zotero's own sidebar icons are single-colour SVGs tinted through
`-moz-context-properties`, and they turn white on the selected row like
everything else. Copying that would have been the tidier answer.

Gecko, however, resolves `context-fill` only for images from `chrome:` and
`resource:` URIs, and a plugin's icon comes out of its XPI: there would have
been nothing to paint with. So the mark brings its own colour, which at least
keeps it legible against the accent background instead of letting it vanish
into it.
